title: GitHub
intro: Let your agents read the code, issues and pull requests of the repositories you list. If you allow it, they can also comment and open issues there.
limits: This connection does not answer @mentions on GitHub yet. An agent works on GitHub only when you ask it in a chat.
name: Name
tokenHelp: Starts with github_pat_. It is kept sealed and never shown again.
tokenSaved: Saved. Type a token to replace it.
tokenShape: Use a fine-grained token: it starts with github_pat_.
tokenSpace: The token has no spaces. Copy it again without the spaces around it.
reposHelp: One per line, as owner/name. {{count}} listed. Any other repository is refused.
reposShape: "{{entry}}" is not written owner/name, for example mudler/LocalAI.
agentOptionalHint: Optional. Without an agent this connection only holds the token, the repository list and the write mode for your chats. It answers no messages and listens for nothing.
checkSeveral: Repository checks run when you have one GitHub connection, because a check from this page cannot tell which one you mean. In a chat, enable the connections in the Tools menu.

check.title: Check of {{name}}
check.unreachable: {{repo}}: this token cannot reach it. Add it to the token's repositories on GitHub.
check.readWrite: {{repo}}: reachable, and the token can write.
check.refused: {{repo}}: GitHub refused this token. Check that it has not expired and that it covers this repository.
check.failed: {{repo}}: the check did not finish. Try again in a moment.

noRepos: No repositories listed: the agent can read none.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.message: The agent can no longer reach these repositories, and the token saved with it is deleted. To set it up again you must enter the token again.

setup.title: How to make the token
setup.linkLabel: Create a token on GitHub (opens in a new tab)
setup.step1: Open GitHub with the button above. Name the token, for example LocalAI, and set an expiry. Ninety days is a good start.
setup.step2: Under Repository access, choose Only select repositories and pick the ones you list here.
setup.step3: Under Permissions, set what the table says for the mode you want. Leave everything else off.
setup.step4: Create the token, copy it and paste it in the token field. GitHub shows it only once.

table.caption: Repository permissions to give the token
table.write: Asks first, or acts without asking

writeMode.label: What the agent may change on GitHub
writeMode.hint: Comments, new issues, labels and closing issues. It never merges, deletes or pushes code.

line.off: It cannot change anything on GitHub.
line.propose: Each change waits for your OK.

note.off: Write access is off: this connection only reads.
note.propose: Each change waits in your approvals until you confirm it. Anything an agent writes is public to everyone who can see the repository.
note.auto: A chat of yours posts the change at once, without asking. Anything the agent writes is public to everyone who can see the repository. Runs without you present still wait for your confirmation.
